raisedBy.description:

recommendation.description: The answer the asker would take by itself, and why; left out where it cannot make the case.

settles.description:
Whether the reply settles the question; left out, it settles where it carries a choice or the question

kinds.description: Event kinds to hear of; empty for every kind.

queueNames.description: Queues to hear of; empty for every queue.

ttlMs.description: The span, 1000 to 86400000; left out, the subscription stands until it is deleted.

choices.description: The answers to choose from; empty for an open question.

toldByAsker.description: Whether the asker puts it before whoever answers it itself, so no consumer of the events tells of it.

QuestionChange.description:
A question paused, opened again, withdrawn or closed unsent; put again in other words; or told how far its
asker has been handed its replies.

heardThrough.description: The last reply the asker was handed.

QuestionPage.description: One page of a list, and whether anything stands past its last member.

QuestionRecommendation.description: The answer an asker would take by itself, and the one line saying why.

answer.description: One of the question's choices, or a free answer where the choices do not cover it.

why.description: The one line saying why that is the answer.

Subscription.description: What a subscriber is told of: events of the kinds listed, narrowed to the queues, scope and items named, an empty list or a null scope matching all. With a url each event is posted there as the subscription-event webhook; without one it is read on GET /events with subscriptionId. A subscription with ttlMs runs out at expiresAt unless a change renews it. A webhook that keeps failing moves it to failing; setting state back to active delivers again from the event after deliveredEventId.

SubscriptionChange.description: A change of a subscription, as a merge patch.

ttlMs.description: Renews the subscription for this span from now; left out, for the span it stands with.

SubscriptionPage.description: One page of a list, and whether anything stands past its last member.

SubscriptionState.description: Whether a subscription is handed its events.

Task.description: A task of a work order.

TaskChange.description: A move of a task, as a merge patch.

TaskPage.description: One page of a list, and whether anything stands past its last member.

steps.description: The lines of the plan, in order; the step at place n is the task of stage n.

state.description: The standing state where left out, or draft for a new work order.

WorkOrderChange.description: A change of a work order, as a merge patch.

info.description: A todo kept as middleware: items, notes, reports, work orders and their tasks, queues, leases on items, questions and their replies, and subscriptions, stored and served through this API and nothing else. The service never executes: it launches no run and calls no other service; the only calls it makes are deliveries to the addresses its subscribers registered. Work reaches whoever does it two ways, side by side: pushed, as the events of a subscription it registered, and pulled, by a lease. Who a member belongs to is opaque to the service: scope and the <role>Name fields are the caller's strings, and labels the caller's metadata.

post.description: Posted to the url the subscriber registered, with the subscription's key in the Job-Subscription header and, where a secret was given, sha256= and the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of the body under it in Job-Signature. A 2xx acknowledges it; anything else is tried again with backoff, and ten failures in a row move the subscription to failing. The subscriber drops an event it has seen by its id.

x-harness.entry: A harness subscribes with job_subscribe to the queues it serves (or names them when it starts the server), and is told of each item opened there by an MCP notification; it takes that item, or the next of a queue, with job_lease_next, reads its brief, notes and work order, hears words appended while it works by the same subscription or job_notes, reports with job_report and closes the item. The server renews the leases and subscriptions it took while its harness runs, and lets them go when it stops.
x-harness.notifications: The MCP server reads its subscriptions in the stream form and sends each event as an MCP notification: notifications/resources/updated on the resource job://items/{itemId} or job://queues/{queueName} the event names, and, where it was started with a channel, the event itself as notifications/<channel> carrying content and meta, for a harness that takes messages pushed into its session.
